title: Model Locker — endpoint seed flows & version-lock UX writeup
content:
Purpose and intent:
This is a compact, practical writeup for a small UI surface we’re calling the "Model Locker": an inline, lightweight overlay that helps users create an endpoint seeded from the catalog and lock a specific model version (or allow automatic upgrades). Aim is to reduce cognitive overhead during endpoint creation while making pin/auto-upgrade tradeoffs explicit.

Audience and persona notes:
- Primary: Platform/ML engineers creating new endpoints for product features (care about predictability and rollout control).
- Secondary: App engineers who need a simple fast path — they prefer a sensible default (auto-upgrade off by default) and clear rollback story.
- SRE/ops: need observability hooks and metrics to be emitted when pin changes happen.

High-level flows covered:
1) Quick-seed: user selects a model from the catalog list -> launches endpoint creation -> Model Locker shows a two-column summary (selected model + recommended variants) -> confirm and create.
2) Pin-after-create: from endpoint detail, open Model Locker modal to switch between "pinned" and "floating" with version selector and rollout policy.
3) Canary/rollout toggle: allow user to create a canary route pointing at a newer model while main route stays pinned.

Wireframe frames (visual descriptions for designers/devs):
- Frame A: Catalog row context menu -> "Create endpoint -> Quick seed". Small slide-over anchored to the row. Left: card with model tile (name, architecture, perf badges: latency@max tokens, token-cost-est). Right: two options: "Create & pin latest" (primary) and "Create & float (auto-upgrade)" (secondary). Microcopy under float: "Allow safe upgrades when compatible; we’ll notify about regressions."
- Frame B: Model Locker expanded (during create). Top: endpoint name input (pre-filled), route path preview, region selector. Middle: version control panel with timeline scrubber showing 3 recent versions and a dropdown "pin to" with commit-ish hash and human label. Bottom: rollout options: Immediate | Canary (10%/30% slider) | Staged (schedule). Primary action: "Create endpoint". Secondary: "Save as blueprint".
- Frame C: Endpoint detail -> small inline badge showing "Pinned: model-2.1.4" with hover menu -> "Change pin" opens lightweight modal with search/filter, diff link to model details.

Microcopy experiments (A/B variants):
- Pin button label variants: 
  A1: "Lock to version"
  A2: "Pin version (recommended)"
  A3: "Freeze model version" (too strong?)
- Float/auto-upgrade variants:
  B1: "Allow automatic upgrades"
  B2: "Auto-upgrade when compatible"
  B3: "Keep up-to-date automatically" (implies less control)
- Tooltip for cost tradeoff: "Pinning fixes behavior but may require manual cost/quality tradeoffs when new optimizations are available."

Error states and recovery flows:
- Create fails due to incompatible quantization profile: inline error under version selector: "Selected build not compatible with chosen runtime. Choose a different build or switch runtime." Recovery: button "Suggest compatible builds" that opens prefiltered catalog.
- Rollout fails mid-canary: modal shows "Canary halted — observed increased hallucination rate vs baseline" with links to evaluation runs and a quick rollback button "Revert canary".
- Conflicting pin change (two users): optimistic UI with toast: "Another user updated pin to model-2.2.0. Review changes? [View diff] [Keep mine]". Add audit log entry and email notification option.

Accessibility and keyboard flows:
- All controls focusable in logical order: model tile -> endpoint name -> version dropdown -> rollout slider -> primary action.
- Keyboard shortcut from endpoint detail to open Model Locker: "G then L" (G = go, L =locker) — discuss whether this is discoverable.
- Ensure screen reader text for pinned badge: "Endpoint pinned to model <name> version <x.y.z>" with link to open locker.

Observability and analytics (events to emit):
- catalog.create_endpoint.click (props: model_id, model_version, region, is_pinned, user_id)
- locker.open_from_endpoint (endpoint_id, current_pin)
- locker.change_pin.attempt (endpoint_id, from_version, to_version, rollout_type)
- locker.pin_conflict.detected (endpoint_id, attempted_by, winner_user)
- rollout.canary.event (endpoint_id, canary_percent, metric_delta_snapshot)
- metrics suggested: time_to_create_endpoint_ms, pin_change_latency_ms, pin_conflicts_per_week

Backlog grooming (candidate tickets with rough story points and priority):
- LR-1201: Implement quick-seed slide-over UX (3pts, P1) owner: Priya
- LR-1202: Version selector component with time-scrubber and diff link (5pts, P1) owner: Diego
- LR-1203: Audit log entries for pin changes + email notification toggle (3pts, P2) owner: Ethan
- LR-1204: Canary rollback helper (safety button + run eval) (5pts, P1) owner: SRE engineering
- LR-1205: Microcopy A/B experiment infra for pin/float labels (2pts, P3) owner: Product growth

Acceptance criteria (for M1):
- Users can create an endpoint directly from a catalog row using the quick-seed flow.
- The creation modal exposes a clear option to pin or float a model and records the choice.
- Pin changes create an auditable event and show conflict to other users.
- Canary rollout can be configured at creation time (10% default) and supports a simple rollback action.

Open design questions and risks:
- Default behavior for auto-upgrade: safety vs velocity. Recommendation: default to pinned for production orgs, float allowed in dev orgs. Need org-level setting.
- How to present model diffs meaningfully? Lightweight metric highlights (latency, eval score deltas) might be enough for 80% of cases.
- Cost signals: when auto-upgrading to a slower but cheaper variant, do we surface cost per 1M tokens as a primary signal? Risk of clutter.

Implementation notes for engineers:
- Reuse catalog model tile component for quick-seed slide-over to minimize new CSS surface.
- Version selector should fetch model-metadata-timeseries endpoint (backend) for last 5 releases to avoid big lists.
- Emit analytics on open + submit; backend should idempotently record pin events for audit.
- Keep slide-over ephemeral: only create endpoint after explicit "Create endpoint" click (no implicit saves).

Next steps and small experiments:
- Design: quick prototype for slide-over + small A/B test for microcopy (A1 vs A2) — 1 week.
- Eng: spike for version-selector performance (client-side caching) — 3 days.
- PM: propose org-level default for pinning + add to onboarding checklist.

Notes to self (scratch):
- Check with research if we can compute a simple "behavior delta" (few metrics) for model diffs — might reduce need for deep evals during UI decision.
- Ask legal about retention policy for audit events for pinned changes (GDPR retention window).
- Consider dark UX: make pinned state visually heavier so users don’t mistake it for default.

Rough copy snippets for final UI (single-line):
- Primary create button: "Create endpoint (pin to current model)"
- Secondary: "Create endpoint and allow auto-upgrades"
- Tooltip on pinned badge: "This endpoint will always use the selected model version until manually changed."

End of doc.
